note: AI steps used a simulated provider server, not a live endpoint.

results.step: A1 keyboard only: Tab to the name field, create a model with Enter, no AI credentials
A2 keyboard only: switch section (Alt+2), focus the add field with "/", add a threat with Enter
B1 add components on the canvas, rename them in the inspector
B2 draw a data flow by dragging between handles (canvas)
B3 the table view offers the same operations without a pointer: add flow, add boundary, set membership
B4 set exposure and flow properties; relationships stay consistent
B5 add a trust boundary from the canvas toolbar (no table needed)
C1 complete a threat: statement fields, targets from the shared model, judgement with reasons
C2 add a mitigation from the threat; implemented and verified need attestation and evidence
C3 assumptions and questions link to model elements
C4 undo and redo reverse a core edit
D1 data survives a page reload and a server restart
D2 saved file is deterministic: reloading and saving again changes nothing
D3 a damaged project file is shown (not hidden) and can be restored from its backup
E1 export native JSON and Markdown; the CLI validates the exported file
E2 Threat Composer export is lossy and says so before download
E3 import a Threat Composer file: preview shows converted and unsupported content, ids preserved
E4 a malformed import is rejected safely
F1 open the demonstration; it is clearly labelled
F2 selecting a threat highlights the architecture elements it affects; selecting a component shows its reasoning
F3 scan a newer source revision (preview) and sync it: no provider contacted
F4 review shows the flagged assumption, threat, mitigation and boundary with the reason and trace
F5 the canvas marks flagged components without relying on colour
F6 close a review item with a rationale; it records a decision and stays closed after re-sync
F7 proposals: edit then accept, dependent mitigation, reject with reason; nothing auto-accepted
F9 "Show on diagram" leaves Review and highlights the connected components
F8 compare two revisions in the UI shows the same deterministic change
G1 configure a provider (simulated endpoint); the model identifier is configuration, not code
G2 AI analysis: disclosure names the host and files; sending requires explicit confirmation
G3 proposal shows reasoning, verified evidence and the assumed-vs-observed split; accept keeps AI provenance
G4 reanalysis preserves human decisions: rejected stays rejected, accepted is not duplicated
G5 provider failure leaves the project usable and says what happened
G6 malformed provider output is rejected safely
G7 cancellation stops the run, leaves the project intact, and does not retry
H1 automated accessibility audit (axe-core) of the main views has no serious or critical violations
H2 responsive: no horizontal page scroll at tablet and phone widths; inspector becomes a drawer
H3 manual modelling made no network requests beyond the local server
H4 no uncaught page errors
